title: French pastry chef crowned world's best aims 'to be world champion every day'
facts: The International Union of Bakers and Confectioners (UIBC) named French chef Benoît Castel World Confectioner of the Year.
Benoît Castel received the UIBC award on July 14, 2026, in Singapore.
Benoît Castel is 54 years old and operates several patisseries in Paris.
French pastry chef Nina Métayer was crowned world champion by the UIBC three years prior to Benoît Castel.
Benoît Castel originates from the Brittany region in western France.
The best-selling pastry item at Benoît Castel's shops is a chocolate choux pastry.
Benoît Castel decorates each of his pastries with a small, scalloped shortbread biscuit.
Fruit and vegetables are supplied to Benoît Castel's bakeries from his personal gardens and orchards in Brittany.
Romain Montbabut serves as the head baker working alongside Benoît Castel.
Romain Montbabut has worked with Benoît Castel for six years.
Benoît Castel opened his independent business in 2012 after working with chef Hélène Darroze, at Hotel Costes, and at La Grande Epicerie de Paris.
Benoît Castel created 'pain du coin', a bread made from multiple flours, quince sourdough starter, honey, and Salish salt.
Benoît Castel created 'the bread of yesterday and tomorrow' made from the prior day's unsold bakery stock.
Benoît Castel collaborates with artists to design specialty Yule log cakes.
Benoît Castel and his daughter Margot are scheduled to open a new bakery-restaurant venue in Paris in September.
